ayat.summary: Exception to human despair/boasting: patient believers doing good receive forgiveness and reward. Potential broad perseverance/reward teachings across traditions; no source-specific direct passage established.

Prophet may feel pressured to omit revelation amid demand for treasure or accompanying angel; messenger is a warner and God a guardian. Context-specific polemic; no precise earlier textual antecedent established.
Challenge to produce ten fabricated surahs like the Qur'an. No traceable pre-Islamic primary-text equivalent established in this screening; avoid inventing a parallel from generic literary contests.
Conditional response to the surah challenge, divine knowledge, exclusive deity and submission. No sufficiently distinctive earlier text established; monotheism alone is too general.

Those seeking worldly life and adornment receive their deeds' recompense here; potential contrast with Matthew's warning about earthly praise and reward. The Qur'anic statement is broader than Matthew's public-display-of-piety context.

candidates.checked_version: New International Version English, Matthew 6:2-6 (online); Matthew 6:16-18 not independently inspected for this record
candidates.similarity: Both discuss immediate earthly reward versus a different divine or ultimate reward.
candidates.difference: Matthew criticizes religious acts performed to gain human admiration, while Qur'an 11:15 addresses people whose objective is worldly life and its adornment; their referents and rhetorical settings differ.
candidates.dating_limits: Matthew is an early Christian text predating Islam, but date of composition is not the date of surviving Greek manuscripts; neither Greek critical apparatus nor versional variants examined.
candidates.limits: English passage inspected; full Greek critical text, textual variants, Matthew 6:16-18, and relevant scholarship pending. Loose motif only, no borrowing claim.
